tagline: A library of our love, candlelit and yours to explore.

pages.text: Candice, from the moment you walked into my life, everything changed. This book holds our moments — the ones I never want to forget.

pages.caption: That smile I still dream about

pages.text: You make ordinary days feel like magic.
Remember when we... well, every time. Here are some of my favorite moments with you.
I'd relive every second with you.
I write these things I can never say out loud. But I want you to know every word.

Dear Candice,

You don't know this, but I watch you when you think no one's looking. The way you tilt your head when you're thinking. The way you laugh — really laugh — with your whole body. That's my favorite sound in the entire world.

I don't need grand adventures. I need quiet mornings with you. I need your hand in mine. I need you.

Forever yours,
Michael
Some words are better written than spoken.
Then speak them again. I want to hear them every time.
This is where we write our next chapter together. What do you want our story to look like?
I promise to choose you every single day.
I promise to never let you forget it.
End of Book 4. But not the end of us. That story is still being written, one day at a time, together.

books.title: Poems that make me think of you

pages.text:
Affection between friends,
and we've been to so many of our funerals
and found our way back.

In uncharted waters
we scratch and claw
trying to love the sadness
out of each other.

(I think it's all gone now my love?)

Late night conversations about everything
and tender kissing reminds us
how we are a secret
in our own little world.

I watch you soothe your children
and it finds me in awe of you
and your maternal instincts,

The tenderness is all inbetween
and all around us.

This time we fight for love.

How can I convince my heart?

How do I tell myself it's going to be alright,
that there will still be parts of me
in tact after you,

That I won't be left a ghost
wondering, waiting
and wishing I was still with you?

Who am I to think that it's not already happened
and that we're in the inevitable state of borrowed time
until forever rears its head?

I sit on your balcony
and let the wind wash over my desire to love you
yet it persists —
you will always persist.

I am lost in thought
(oh my love, to get lost with you)

I ask what type of man you consider me to be
(I am yours, I am yours)

and mostly I question
if my name is anything more than a metaphor
for almost.

I've loved you —
(and I shouldn't be ashamed of it)
longer than I can remember

with a fondness that feels
like your body pressed against mine

with a tension so palpable
that it's felt across oceans

and there's no question
whether or not you're the sun.
